newsitem.title: USA: New York Times to get 3 new board members.
newsitem.headline: New York Times to get 3 new board members.

text.p: Three longtime members of the New York Times Co's board of directors, including International Business Machines Corp Chairman and Chief Executive Louis Gerstner, have decided not to seek re-election.

Also stepping down from the board when their terms are up are Marian Sulzberger Heiskell, the sister of Times Chairman and Chief Executive Arthur Ochs Sulzberger, and former Secretary of State Cyrus Vance, the Times said Thursday.
"It's time to bring younger board members on the board," Times spokeswoman Nancy Nielsen said.
Heiskell, who is 78, has been on the board for 34 years; Vance, who is 80, has served 18 years on the board; Gerstner, 55, has been a board member for 11 years.

President and Chief Operating Officer Russell Lewis, 49, and Times publisher Arthur Sulzberger, 45, have been nominated to the board. The board's nominating committee is seeking a candidate for the remaining spot on the 15-member board.
The elections are to be held at the Times' annual meeting in May.
((-- Lisa Marie Pane, New York newsdesk, 212-859-1713))
